source_text: Quotiens aliquid beatissimi martyres dei omnipotentis et Christi eius festinantes ad promissa regna caelorum carissimis suis uerecundius mandant, memores humilitatis quae semper in fide solet facere maiores, quanto modestius petiuerunt, tanto efficacius impetrauerunt. Et nobis quoque hoc praedicandae gloriae suae munus dei testes nobilissimi reliquerunt, Marianum dico, ex dilectissimis fratribus nostris, et Iacobum, quos mihi scitis praeter communem sacramenti religionem, uitae etiam societate et domesticis affectibus inhaesisse. Qui contra saeuientis saeculi pressuras et gentiles impetus habituri tam sublime certamen, praelium suum, quod instinctu spiritus caelestis inierunt, in notitiam fraternitatis per nos uenire iusserunt, non quod in terris uellent coronae suae gloriam per iactantiam praedicari, sed ut praecedentibus experimentis multitudo plebis et dei populus ad exemplum fidei posset armari. Nec inmerito id obsecuturo mihi fiducia familiaris iniunxit. Quis enim dubitet quae nobis in pace uitae communitas fuerit, quando nos indiuidua dilectione uiuentes unum tempus persecutionis inuenerit?
thought_title: Asking a Friend to Publish Their Contest
orientation: The narrator, a close friend of Marian and James, opens by explaining that they ordered him to bring their struggle to the knowledge of the brotherhood.
pass_a_gloss: Whenever the most blessed martyrs of almighty God and of his Christ, hastening to the promised kingdoms of the heavens, entrust anything to their dearest ones rather modestly, mindful of the humility which in faith is always accustomed to make greater, by how much more modestly they have asked, by so much more effectively they have obtained. And to us also the most noble witnesses of God have left this task of proclaiming their glory, I mean Marian, from our most beloved brothers, and James, whom you know to have clung to me beyond the common religion of the solemn pledge, also by partnership of life and by affections of the household. Who, about to have so sublime a contest against the pressures of a raging age and pagan attacks, ordered their battle, which they entered by impulse of the heavenly spirit, to come to the knowledge of the brotherhood through us, not because on earth they wished the glory of their crown to be proclaimed through boasting, but so that by preceding examples the multitude of the people and the people of God could be armed toward an example of faith. Nor undeservedly has familiar trust enjoined this on me as one about to obey. For who would doubt what community of life was to us in the peace of life, when one time of persecution has found us living with undivided love?

pass_b_english: Whenever the most blessed martyrs of almighty God and his Christ race toward the promised kingdom of heaven and entrust some charge to their dearest friends, they ask with modesty. They remember the humility that always makes men greater in faith, and the more modestly they ask, the more surely their request is granted.

These noblest witnesses of God have left to me also the task of proclaiming their glory. I mean Marian, one of our dearest brothers, and James. You know how closely they clung to me, not only through our shared life under the solemn pledge but through daily companionship and deep family affection.

They were about to face so great a contest against the crushing pressures of a raging age and pagan attack. They commanded that their battle, which they entered at the prompting of the heavenly Spirit, should come to the knowledge of our brothers and sisters through me. They did not want the glory of their crown proclaimed on earth out of boasting. They wanted the whole congregation, God's people, to be armed for the pattern of faith by the trials that went before them. Our close friendship rightly laid this obedient task upon me. For who could doubt what fellowship was ours in the peace of our life together, when a single season of persecution found us living in undivided love?
